Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships
San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA

About Anthropic

Anthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As the Manager of the Partnerships Applied AI Solutions Architect team, you will drive adoption of frontier AI by enabling deployment of Anthropic's products (Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, API) through our Global and Regional System Integrators, cloud partners (AWS, GCP, Azure), and strategic technology partners.

You will build and lead a team of Partner Solutions Architects, establish processes and best practices for partner-led pre-sales engagements, and represent Anthropic as the technical lead on its most important partnerships. In collaboration with Sales, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering, you will help partners incorporate leading-edge AI into their practices, accelerate indirect revenue, and execute long-term GTM strategy while maintaining our best-in-class safety standards.

Responsibilities

    Team Leadership & Development: Hire, manage, and mentor a team of Partner Solutions Architects. Set goals, run reviews, and coach each team member toward high productivity and career growth.
    Strategic Technical Partnership: Act as the senior technical thought partner to Anthropic's GTM partnerships team. Co-build partner strategy with aligned GTM leadership, drive key programs, and align cross-functional stakeholders (Sales, Product, Engineering) behind partner outcomes.
    Partner Enablement & Ecosystem: Embed your team with GSI and cloud partner technical teams to enable their AI practices, troubleshoot, and evangelize Anthropic in their developer communities. Represent Anthropic at partner events (GSI workshops, AWS/GCP summits, hackathons) and contribute technical content and thought leadership.
    Joint Solution Development: Lead partners in identifying high-value, industry-specific GenAI applications. Develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures and best practices to accelerate time to deployment.
    Customer Deal Support: Own the technical portion of partner-led pre-sales engagements. Intervene directly on strategic deals where partners are the primary delivery vehicle, providing deep solution architecture guidance.
    Product Feedback: Gather and validate feedback on Anthropic's products from partner deployments and deliver it to Product and Engineering to inform roadmap and partner strategy.

You may be a good fit if you have

    7+ years in technical customer-facing or partner-facing roles (Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Partner SE, TAM).
    3+ years managing pre-sales or partner-facing technical teams; comfortable building foundational teams in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
    Track record building and scaling partnerships with GSIs (e.g., Accenture, Deloitte, TCS, Infosys) and/or cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure).
    Deep understanding of partner-led selling and delivery: indirect revenue models, enablement at scale, and joint GTM motions.
    Technical depth in enterprise AI deployments: LLM architecture, prompt engineering, evaluation, API integrations, and production use cases.
    Exceptional communication and executive presence; able to build trusted relationships with C-suite, partner leadership, and engineering teams alike.
    A love of teaching and mentoring, and a passion for advancing safe, beneficial AI.

Strong candidates may also have

    5+ years leading partner-facing SA teams through hypergrowth, including developing both senior and junior talent.
    Direct experience helping GSIs or consultancies build their AI/ML practice - enablement programs, certification paths, joint solution development.

Compensation

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role's On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary: $315,000 - $380,000 USD

# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000–$380,000 OTE | Reports to Partnerships (partner-facing technical GTM) |

## JD Complement
Anthropic’s ecosystem opportunity is to turn a safety-oriented AI platform into dependable enterprise outcomes delivered through third parties.

The core tension is reach versus consistency. Service firms and cloud allies can extend technical capacity, vertical expertise, and customer access, yet every indirect deployment must reflect clear product boundaries, sound governance,
and a credible user experience.

This position appears to sit between commercial expansion and implementation discipline: making Claude practical in complex environments while converting recurring field signals into actionable internal learning.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic is an AI research and public-benefit company focused on systems that are dependable, understandable, and controllable. That orientation makes trust a product attribute as well as a company value.

Its business spans individual use, enterprise adoption, and developer integration. Claude therefore serves distinct audiences whose needs overlap around security, workflow fit, administration, and confidence in real-world use.

The operating model must translate rapidly changing model capabilities into patterns that enterprise customers can understand, deploy, govern, and extend. External delivery capacity is valuable only if it reinforces rather than fragments
those patterns.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Anthropic’s emphasis on safety can be commercially differentiating when buyers need both capability and assurance. For enterprise stakeholders, the architecture conversation is likely to include practical questions about access,
data boundaries, implementation risk, and operational accountability.

Claude addresses knowledge work, analysis, software development, and organizational problem-solving. This broad applicability creates pressure to distinguish reusable solutions from narrowly customized projects that cannot scale
across customers or partners.

Enterprise success depends on more than provisioned access. It includes organizational readiness, user adoption, administrative controls, workflow selection, and a way to learn from production usage.

A central leadership challenge will be establishing decision paths for partner questions: what can be resolved through published guidance, what needs expert intervention, and what should become a product or platform priority.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
The most relevant internal stakeholders likely span commercial, technical, and trust-oriented functions rather than a single reporting chain.

- Partnerships leaders need an ecosystem that expands market coverage while maintaining disciplined economics and clear accountability.
- Revenue teams need technical support that improves customer confidence without creating an unsustainable custom-services model.
- Product and engineering teams need structured evidence on repeatable adoption barriers, not isolated requests from individual accounts.
- Customer administrators and implementation sponsors need predictable paths from initial use cases to broader organizational adoption.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Claude is positioned for both business users and developers, which makes enterprise architecture broader than API integration. Practical deployments may involve identity, permissions, organizational data, user workflows,
administrative configuration, change enablement, and ongoing measurement.

Anthropic’s enterprise materials emphasize security and compliance alongside capabilities for teams building with AI. That signals an environment where solution credibility depends on operational design, not model demonstrations alone.

The strongest architecture assets are likely to be reusable and opinionated: tested patterns, discovery frameworks, readiness criteria, governance guidance, integration approaches, and clear limits on unsupported customization.

The key platform question is not simply where a model can be applied. It is how customers can introduce AI into consequential processes while preserving control, user trust, and measurable business value.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
The ecosystem is strategically important because consultancies, integrators, cloud providers, and technology partners can increase deployment capacity while bringing industry context and existing customer relationships.

Public material around Accenture and Anthropic points to an enterprise implementation relationship centered on productivity, value creation, and new digital offerings. This suggests a services-enabled go-to-market model rather than
a basic referral or resale arrangement.

A durable ecosystem motion will need to combine:

- Technical education that equips partner practitioners to use approved implementation methods with confidence.
- Joint offerings that connect broad AI capability to repeatable industry, functional, or workflow problems.
- Technical engagement models for high-stakes opportunities where architecture quality influences commercial momentum.
- Deployment-feedback processes that surface recurring friction, adoption gaps, and missing platform capabilities.
- Explicit ownership boundaries across partner delivery, customer operations, platform behavior, security requirements, and roadmap choices.
- Quality mechanisms that prevent a fast-growing partner base from producing inconsistent customer experiences.

## Recent Events & Urgency
Anthropic’s presence across enterprise and developer contexts raises the value of consistent partner execution. As more organizations seek governed production use rather than experimentation, implementation quality becomes a
commercial and reputational issue.

The availability of enterprise administration and adoption resources suggests that Anthropic views rollout as a repeatable operating discipline. Partners must be able to connect technical configuration with user readiness and
organizational change.

The market pressure is to help customers realize useful outcomes quickly without trading away trust. For Anthropic, that makes ecosystem architecture a meaningful lever for both growth and responsible deployment.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Build partner-facing technical organizations that turn a sophisticated AI platform into repeatable enterprise outcomes.
- Create enablement systems for consultancies, integrators, cloud alliances, and technical delivery communities.
- Establish practical architecture standards that balance customer flexibility with product consistency and governance.
- Lead complex technical conversations across partner executives, customer stakeholders, commercial teams, and product builders.
- Translate field patterns into prioritized platform insights instead of allowing bespoke account demands to dominate.
- Develop scalable solution assets for security-conscious, production-oriented AI adoption.
- Coach technical talent through ambiguity while creating clear operating rhythms, quality bars, and escalation routes.
- Treat responsible implementation as an architectural and commercial advantage, not a compliance afterthought.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Anthropic appears to need partner scale without losing the implementation discipline that supports its trust-centered market position.
- A useful discussion could focus on how reusable deployment patterns reduce friction for customers while improving partner autonomy.

## Do Not Use As Proof
The JD and this briefing are targeting inputs only. Candidate claims, metrics, leadership examples, partnership results, and technical accomplishments must come from the governed resume/proof graph.
